newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germans advised to leave Central African Republic.
newsitem.headline: Germans advised to leave Central African Republic.

text.p: Germany on Thursday advised its citizens in the Central African Republic to leave the country after recent clashes between African peacekeepers and army mutineers which killed at least 80 people.

The Foreign Ministry, in a statement released in Bonn, also warned Germans against travelling to the Central African Republic. Earlier on Thursday, Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel ordered the German embassy in Bangui to close temporarily.

"The Foreign Ministry once again urgently calls on all Germans in the Central African Republic to leave the country without delay. We warn against journeys to the Central African Republic," the ministry statement said.
A ministry spokesman said Bonn had told citizens to leave earlier this year when trouble previously flared in the country but had later advised it was safe to return.
Fighting erupted last week between the disaffected soldiers and the peacekeepers, deployed to the Central African Republic to help restore peace after three army mutinies in under a year.
Witnesses in Bangui said fighting had broken out again on Thursday, with the two sides exchanging automatic arms fire.
